---
title: "8.1 Purpose and use"
order: 1
---

## The question it answers

A small business that is using most of its credit line is either growing into it or running
out of room. Proactive Line Increase asks which booked accounts the bank should **offer more
credit before they ask**: accounts that are good for it, constrained by the limit they have,
and profitable to lend more to. It is the bank's only module that adds exposure on its own
initiative, which is why most of what it does is say no.

Its target is `{{< var li.target >}}`: whether an account is a good candidate for an
increase, as the generator defines it ([8.2](data.qmd#li-label)). The model ranks the book on
that label; three rules then decide who is actually offered anything, and how much.

## The output

`score_population` (`line_increase/src/candidates.py`) scores every booked account and
returns, for each:

| Output | What it is |
|---|---|
| `prob` | the candidate model's probability of `{{< var li.target >}}`, rounded for display; eligibility is decided on the unrounded value |
| `recommended_amount` | the increase the amount rules give: the lowest of three caps, floored at zero and rounded ([8.3](methodology.qmd#li-amount)) |
| `incremental_ead`, `incremental_roe`, `incremental_net_income`, `clears_hurdle` | the increase priced by the pricing engine: its assumed drawn exposure, its return on equity, and whether that return clears the hurdle ([8.3](methodology.qmd#li-roe)) |
| `eligible` | **the offer**: the probability is above the offer threshold, the scorecard's PD is within the risk appetite, the amount is positive, and the increment clears the hurdle — all four |
| `top_shap_reasons` | the three features pushing the probability up most, by SHAP value |

`candidates` ranks the `eligible` accounts by probability and returns them; `segments` rolls
offers and incremental exposure up by score band and industry.

**An offer is `eligible`, never a positive amount.** Over the booked book
{{< var li.n_amount_positive >}} accounts have `recommended_amount > 0`, and
{{< var li.n_offered >}} are eligible: {{< var li.amount_offer_ratio >}} accounts with an
amount for every offer. `candidates()` is the authority, and every count of offers in this
chapter is its count.

### The funnel {#li-funnel}

The four clauses, in the order `score_population` ANDs them, over the
{{< var li.n_book >}} booked accounts:

{{< include ../../_generated/li-funnel.md >}}

![The offer funnel over the booked book: each clause of `eligible`, in order.](fig/offer-funnel.svg){#fig-offer-funnel}

The model's threshold removes most of the book, the PD ceiling and the amount rules most of
the rest, and the ROE test removes {{< var li.funnel.roe.dropped >}} of the
{{< var li.funnel.amount.n >}} that remain. What survives is
{{< var li.offer_share >}} of the book.

## The population it is for

The booked book: the {{< var li.n_book >}} accounts the bank lent to
([D2](../d2-data.qmd#two-populations-applicants-and-booked)). An applicant has no on-book
utilisation and no limit to raise. The model is trained and gated on a split of that same
book, and the portal then scores the whole book, including the {{< var li.n_train >}} accounts
the model was fitted on; what that does to the offers is finding 2 ([8.7](limitations.qmd)).

## Who consumes it, and how

Every consumer reads the batch `score_population` computes once at start-up (`app/main.py`).
None re-implements a clause, a cap or the ROE test.

| Consumer | What it takes |
|---|---|
| Portal (v1), `/api/line-increase/summary` | the cohort figures and held-out metrics recorded at training (`metadata.json`), the offer threshold, and `segments` over the scored book |
| Portal (v1), `/api/line-increase/candidates` | `candidates` over the scored book, with the endpoint's own default length (`n: int = 25`, the top {{< var li.portal_n >}}); the v1 page requests the top {{< var li.page_n >}} (`app/static/index.html`) |
| Portal (v1), `/api/line-increase/{business_id}` | one account's probability, eligibility, amount and incremental economics |
| Portal (v1), `/api/dashboard/summary` and `/api/customer/{business_id}` | the number offered and the aggregate incremental ROE recorded at training; one account's eligibility, amount and incremental ROE in the customer-360 view, beside its Early Warning tier |
| Loan workbench (v2), `/api/v2/loan/{business_id}/line-increase` | the three caps with the binding one marked, the steps from the lowest cap to the amount, the four clauses of `eligible` each with its value and threshold, and the increment's profit waterfall (`app/v2/line_increase.py`, `app/v2/li_amounts.py`) |
| Loan workbench (v2), `/api/v2/loans?li_eligible=` | the batch verdict as a facet: the loan list filtered to offers (`app/v2/loans.py`) |

The workbench explains the verdict; it never decides it. Its clauses are recomputed from the
unrounded probability and PD so that the clause it marks as failing is the one that failed,
and `eligible` is always the batch's ([8.9](gate.qmd#li-workbench)). There is no what-if for
line increase: a reviewer cannot move a threshold or a cap and see the book re-scored.

Line Increase reads the scorecard's PD ([8.2](data.qmd#li-score-input)) and the pricing
engine ([8.3](methodology.qmd#li-roe)). It does not read Early Warning; the two meet only in
the customer-360 view, where an offered account can carry an Early Warning tier and triggers
([8.5](performance.qmd#li-ews)).

## Prohibited uses

| Use | Why it is prohibited |
|---|---|
| Counting accounts with a positive `recommended_amount` as offers | An offer is `eligible`; {{< var li.n_amount_not_offered >}} accounts with an amount are not offered. |
| Quoting the offered cohort's label rate, or the candidates list's, as evidence of accuracy | Most offers, and almost all of the list the portal serves, are the model's training rows (finding 2, [8.7](limitations.qmd)). Quote the held-out figures in [8.5](performance.qmd). |
| Reading the cohort gates as evidence that the offers are good | {{< var li.cohort_gate.n_cannot_fail >}} of the {{< var li.gate.n_gates >}} gates cannot fail on this book (finding 1). |
| Reading `incremental_ead` as the exposure the bank commits | It assumes the increase is drawn at today's utilisation; the committed increase is larger (finding 5). |
| Raising a limit without a credit officer's review | The output is an offer list to review, not an approval; it was not validated as a credit decision. |
| Changing `LINE_INCREASE["roe_hurdle"]` to change the hurdle | The module never reads it (finding 4). |
| Any decision about a real business or a real book | The model was fitted to synthetic data, and its label has no real-world definition yet (finding 6; [D1](../d1-purpose.qmd#prohibited-uses)). |
